![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130455/assets/fb482ddbb5bde83cfd6ed383b0f321cb27377f34aafcb9e74e44d91824dcf366.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ is the path comprising of a line segment and a semicircle of radius $1,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=-3$ and ${x}_{1}=2.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=(-3)-2=-5.
$$
